newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower early Wednesday amid increased marketings as drenching rains in the western Corn Belt stalled corn planting and freed producers to sell hogs, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Several buyers in central and western Iowa reported being out of the market following heavy movement late Tuesday and early Wednesday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.50 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 at plants.
Indiana hogs sold steady early, but prices could weaken if and when marketings increase, buyers there said. Hogs in the country sold at $54.50 to $55.00, and at plants $56.50-$58.50.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants.
Rain reportedly was heavy in most of Iowa and moving into western and central Illinois and Wisconsin, sources said.
But prices declines from large marketings should be curbed by a firm tone to pork prices, livestock sources said.
Pork cut-out values on Tuesday were quoted up $0.23 to $0.36 per cwt, USDA reported.
